purpose: Dutasteride is used to treat an enlarged prostate gland in men, a condition called benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). It helps shrink the prostate over time, making it easier to urinate. In some cases, it may also be used to help prevent prostate surgery or treat hair loss in men.
how_it_works: Your body makes a hormone called DHT (dihydrotestosterone) that causes your prostate to grow larger. Dutasteride blocks the enzyme that turns testosterone into DHT, so less DHT is made. With less DHT, your prostate slowly shrinks and your urinary symptoms improve over several months.
common_side_effects: Some men notice a lower sex drive, trouble getting or keeping an erection, or a decrease in the amount of semen released during sex. You may also notice breast tenderness or slight breast enlargement. These effects are usually mild and often improve over time.
warnings: Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant should never handle this medication, especially if the capsule is broken or leaking, as it can cause birth defects in a male baby. Dutasteride lowers your PSA level, which is a blood test used to screen for prostate cancer, so always remind your doctor you are taking this medication. Do not donate blood while taking this drug or for at least 6 months after stopping it.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 0.5 mg capsule taken by mouth once a day. You can take it with or without food, but swallow it whole — do not crush or chew it. It may take 3 to 6 months before you notice improvement in your symptoms, so be patient and keep taking it as directed.
